Encoder-only models see both left and right context and are well suited to classification, tagging, and pooled retrieval representations. Decoder-only models use a causal mask and learn next-token prediction. Encoder–decoder models encode an input bidirectionally and generate an output with causal decoding plus cross-attention. Decoder-only models offer a simple common training/generation objective and flexible prompting at scale; that practical success does not establish universal architectural superiority. A bi-encoder can precompute document vectors and score queries with dot products, avoiding token-by-token generation. [4](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.10084) Encoder–decoders remain useful when input conditioning and output generation have distinct roles. Compare quality at matched data/compute, latency, context size, and output requirements rather than assuming one architecture wins every task.
